Proof.caption: This is the whole product — one timeline, and a conversation that remembers it.
Proof.userMsg: The wedding's Wednesday. Help me with the speech?
Proof.agentMsg: Keep it short and honest — one real moment is enough. During the final, at Marcus's watch party, you saw the two of them finish each other's sentences, and you just knew. That's your opening. And if you want one beat of humor: he was the first person to tell you the truth about your MVP — 'a magic trick'. Short, personal, done.

Act1.title: Time, not threads.
Act1.body: No conversation windows to lose. One timeline of dated slices — and strands that thread related moments across months, converging at NOW.

beats.title: Dinner at Priya's
beats.desc: A small dinner, a few friends, and someone new named Alex — who also runs. You stay until the staff start cleaning up.

beats.title: 5K under 35
beats.desc: From winded on the stairs to 34:47 — it started with the Olympic marathon on TV last summer. Alex high-fives you at the end.

beats.title: Mom's health scare
beats.desc: Nothing life-threatening — but the call you kept postponing can't wait anymore. Weekly calls become non-negotiable.

beats.title: First camping gear, together
beats.desc: A tent, two sleeping pads, one shared budget. The first trip goes on the calendar.

beats.title: The little tool grows up
beats.desc: The weekly-review tool hits a milestone — real users, real feedback. The CSV script from 2024 is unrecognizable now.

beats.title: Half-marathon, finished
beats.desc: Sixteen weeks of training, one bad knee behind you. Alex is at the finish line — exactly where they said they'd be.

beats.title: The best-man speech
beats.desc: Marcus gets married Wednesday. Draft #5 keeps getting deleted — until one night of the final becomes the whole speech.

Act2.title: Three timelines.
Act2.body: Most of your day was only ever lived by you. Most of my thinking only ever happens in deep reads. What we share is the line in the middle — every conversation, every decision, every unspoken moment that got remembered.

Act3.title: A memory that learns.
Act3.body: A compact user card that evolves as you talk — corrected when wrong, refined when things change. Not a dossier. Just what matters.

Act4.title: No black box.
Act4.body: Recall runs in the open. A fast worker scans slice summaries and returns pointers; the main model deep-reads what matters. Every step is visible.
Act4.query: What should I say at Marcus's wedding?
Act4.answerLabel: Marcus was the first to tell you the truth about your MVP — 'a magic trick', conclusions with no reasoning. And on the night of the final, at his watch party, you saw the two of them finish each other's sentences and just knew they'd make it. The brief was short — so tell that one moment. Ninety seconds of honesty beats five minutes of sap.

Act5.title: Specialists, not brute force.
Act5.body: Dynamic context means complex work shouldn't be brute-forced by one model. The main agent orchestrates, dispatching tasks to dedicated agents — recall, reasoning, search, curation. Every dispatch is visible.

cards.title: Your memory, your repository.
cards.body: The slice from the night of August 7 is a Markdown file in your own GitHub repo — along with what the agent was thinking at the time. So is every other moment. No proprietary database, no one else's server.

cards.title: It works while you're away.
cards.body: Close the tab mid-turn. The run is durable and resumable — it keeps going, and when you're back it picks up exactly where it left off.

cards.title: Open source. Self-host. No lock-in.
cards.body: MIT licensed, no telemetry. Run it on your own machine, read every line, keep your memory in your repo. Forever yours.
